elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: 11.2: "Harpoon shall indemnify AbbVie, its Affiliates and its and their respective directors, officers, employees, and agents ... and defend and save each of them harmless" — an express defence duty running to Customer and its Affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: 11.2 covers "any and all Losses in connection with any and all Third Party Claims incurred by or rendered against the AbbVie Indemnitees"; "Third Party Claims" is defined in 11.1 as suits, investigations, claims or demands of Third Parties.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: The operative trigger list in 11.2 is "arising from or occurring as a result of: [***]". The scope is redacted; Section 7.4 ("Infringement Claims by Third Parties") is truncated mid-sentence and only contextually cross-refers to 11.2, so IP coverage cannot be confirmed from the rendered text.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: 11.2's enumerated triggers are redacted ("[***]"); no other rendered provision states an indemnity for Harpoon's breach of Applicable Law.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: 11.2's triggers are redacted; the rendered text contains no confidentiality/data-breach indemnity trigger, and the Article 9 reference relied on sits in the 11.5 damages exclusion, which is not rendered as an indemnity trigger.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: 11.2's triggers are redacted; gross negligence/wilful misconduct appear (per the rationale) only as a carve-out to the consequential-damages exclusion in 11.5, which is not an indemnity trigger.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: 11.3: "The Indemnified Party shall give the indemnifying Party prompt written notice (an \"Indemnification Claim Notice\") of any Losses ... upon which such Indemnified Party intends to base a request for indemnification under this Article 11".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: 11.4.1: "at its option, the indemnifying Party may assume the defense of any Third Party Claim by giving written notice to the Indemnified Party within [***] after ... receipt of an Indemnification Claim Notice" — control is allocated to the indemnifying Party at its election (redacted period is timing only, not the allocation).

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: 11.4.4: the Indemnified Party "shall ... cooperate in the defense or prosecution thereof and shall furnish such records, information and testimony ... as may be reasonably requested".

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: 11.1 (AbbVie's indemnity of the Harpoon Indemnitees) also ends "arising from or occurring as a result of: [***]"; the scope of Customer's exposure is redacted and cannot be confirmed as narrow.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Same defect as the preferred IP element: 11.2's trigger list is redacted, so no IP-infringement trigger is visible in operative text.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: an exclusion for Customer modifications is allowed but not required, so the absence (or unknown presence within the redacted 11.2 triggers) of such a carve-out does not defeat the element; no rendered language contradicts it.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no rendered exclusion appears and none is required. Condition does not apply because Vendor is merely permitted, not obliged, to carve out combination-based infringement.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; the rendered text contains no specification-based carve-out, and its absence is neutral-to-favourable for Customer.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: No procure/modify/replace mechanic appears in rendered Article 11; Section 7.4 ("Infringement Claims by Third Parties") is truncated mid-sentence and Sections 7.5/7.6 are cross-referenced in 11.4.1 but not rendered, so the existence of such remedies cannot be resolved.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund-on-failure-of-remedies language is rendered; the potentially relevant Sections 7.4–7.6 are truncated or absent from the rendered text.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No monetary cap or super-cap of any kind appears in the rendered Article 11; the only rendered limitation architecture is the mutual consequential-damages exclusion referenced in 11.5, which sets no 3x-annual-fees indemnity cap.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: Duplicate check: nothing in 11.1–11.4.4 or any rendered provision expresses a numeric multiple of annual fees limiting Harpoon's indemnity.

reasons: No operative redline is proposed, so no minimality or intent defect arises; nothing favourable (including the Article 11 indemnity architecture and the 11.5 carve-out for indemnified Third Party amounts) is disturbed.

The preferred level is not complete: four elements (IP infringement, Vendor breach of applicable law, Vendor-caused data breach, Vendor gross negligence/wilful misconduct) and the narrow-Customer-indemnity element all depend on the redacted trigger lists in 11.2 and 11.1 ("arising from or occurring as a result of: [***]"). A level cannot be marked complete on inferred scope.

The fallback level is not complete: the IP indemnity itself is unverifiable, the procure/modify/replace and refund remedies are not present in any rendered text, and the 3x-annual-fees super-cap is affirmatively absent from Article 11.

The structural elements are genuinely satisfied and should not be re-drafted: 11.2 supplies an express defend-and-indemnify duty to AbbVie and its Affiliates for Third Party Claims; 11.3 supplies notice; 11.4.1 allocates defence control; 11.4.4 requires reasonable cooperation. Any insertion must not duplicate these.

Actionable next step: request the unredacted 11.1 and 11.2 trigger lists. If 11.2 lacks an IP trigger, insert a discrete new subsection under 11.2 limited to Third Party Claims alleging that the Licensed Compounds, Licensed Products or Harpoon Technology infringe or misappropriate Third Party intellectual property, plus (if still short) triggers for Harpoon's breach of Applicable Law, Harpoon-caused unauthorised access to or disclosure of AbbVie Confidential Information/data, and Harpoon's gross negligence or wilful misconduct — drafted as additions to the existing list so 11.3/11.4 procedure is not duplicated.

If 11.1 is unredacted and sweeps beyond AbbVie-supplied materials/information and AbbVie's breach of Applicable Law, narrow it in the same pass; do not propose narrowing language before the trigger text is available, as a blind edit risks contradicting retained redacted terms.

Note for the file: this is not walk-away territory (no one-way Customer indemnity), so any communication should be framed as a scope confirmation request rather than a deviation notice until the redacted triggers are seen.

The 'needs_review' status is the correct disposition on the rendered record; do not upgrade to compliant on the strength of the Section 7.4 cross-reference, which is inference rather than operative indemnity text.
